headline: Six peptides.
Zero FDA approvals.
dek: HHS opened compounding to BPC-157 and five others. It didn’t approve them.

paragraphs: On October 30, HHS said it won’t take action against licensed pharmacies and physicians that compound BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, MOTS-c, Epitalon and Semax, as long as they meet ten conditions.

The notice, signed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., was filed with the Federal Register on October 28 and published on October 30 under Docket HHS-OASH-2026-0496. It covers state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities and licensed physicians. The public can comment for two weeks after publication.

This is enforcement discretion, not approval. None of the six is FDA-approved, and the policy says so. It does not add them to FDA’s list of ingredients pharmacies may compound with, it is not binding on HHS, and HHS says it may revisit the policy if a safety signal or product-quality problem appears. It runs while FDA writes rules on each peptide.
Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved either. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

The policy follows a July meeting of FDA’s Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee. The committee reviewed seven peptides and recommended six of them; it rejected the seventh, emideltide. FDA’s own career scientists had recommended against all seven. On BPC-157, the vote was 8 to 6, with one abstention. These vote details are as reported by Healio from the July 23–24, 2026 meeting. FDA has not posted the official vote record.

The human record behind BPC-157 is five published studies, about 80 people, and none longer than two weeks. Every one of them is listed, study by study, in [[/bpc-157|the BPC-157 file]]. The other five peptides have files too: [[/tb-500|TB-500]], [[/kpv|KPV]], [[/mots-c|MOTS-c]], [[/epitalon|Epitalon]] and [[/semax|Semax]].

The registries add little. The only ClinicalTrials.gov entry for TB-500, NCT07487363, sponsored by Hudson Biotech and first posted March 23, 2026, describes itself as fictional; the same sponsor registered the BPC-157 hamstring trial cited in the BPC-157 file. And the HHS policy covers only the routes it lists: injection under the skin or into muscle for BPC-157, TB-500, MOTS-c and Epitalon; by mouth or on the skin for BPC-157 and KPV; in the nose for Semax. Each product may hold one active ingredient from the list, and blends are not covered.

pull.quote: We found no studies that administered BPC-157 to humans via the proposed oral, SC, nasal, or transdermal ROA.
